interpretation: In Paul's Areopagus speech, God has fixed a day on which he will judge the world by a man he appointed (hōrisen), 'having given assurance (pistin parascheōn) to all by raising him from the dead'. In context (17.18) the man is Jesus, whose resurrection Paul was preaching. Read as: God's raising of Jesus is God's own confirmation, offered to all, of Jesus' appointment by God, i.e. of his holding a mandate from God. The source is a commitment of the Lukan narrative, not evidence that the resurrection occurred. Limits: the appointment named is to judge; the verse says nothing of founding a society or of teaching (those are the separate premises STMT-MANDATE-COVERS-JESUS-FOUNDING-WITH-TEACHING and STMT-ENVOY-FOUNDING-IS-GODS-FOUNDING). The statement's antecedents (classical attributes, recognizable revelation, Jesus' own claim) only weaken it; its universal over every being satisfying them follows the skeleton's pattern, while the source speaks of the one God who made the world (17.24). A rival rendering of pistis as 'faith' God offers to all still grounds that offer in the resurrection, but would make the verse speak of the hearers' response rather than God's confirmation; on that rendering the claim would not hold and the premise would rest on the other witnesses only.
